relevance_note: The paper describes an infant and her father with a TNFAIP3 nonsense variant: 'The variant was confirmed by Sanger sequencing in the infant and her father.'
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; a short Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON from values I chose by reading, and checked spans. Tables 1 and 2 are laboratory tables for the proband only (tests as rows; Table 2 columns are ages '2 mon' to '20 mon'); lab-row spans quote the test label through the relevant cells. Individuals: the proband (infant), her father (carries the same TNFAIP3 variant, symptomatic), her mother (autoantibody-tested, negative) and 'Her grandmother' (ankylosing spondylitis-like disease; side of family not stated; not genotyped). The mother's TNFAIP3 genotype is not stated; Fig. 2 only says the variant was inherited from the father. Contradictions/ambiguities: (1) pathogenicity: Case description says 'definite pathogenic mutation' and abstract 'pathogenic variant', but the Discussion says 'likely pathogenic variant'; both recorded. (2) 'Her latest laboratory tests (Table 1)' although Table 1 is titled initial laboratory tests; age at last evaluation taken from the last Table 2 column (20 mon). (3) Anti-La is listed among 'positive autoantibodies' in the text but is 'Borderline' in both tables; recorded observed with the Borderline detail. (4) Discussion 'she tested negative for maternal autoantibodies' has an ambiguous referent (the infant had positive anti-Ro); not used. Decisions: n_patients_reported=2 is counted from 'confirmed by Sanger sequencing in the infant and her father', not a number the authors print. No functional assay was done (authors: 'no additional functional study is necessary'; MutationTaster and conservation scores are in silico only), so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported'. Father's zygosity and the NF1 variant type were not stated, so 'not reported'. Low C3/C4 and Hb 9.8 g/dL appear only as numbers without a stated interpretation and were not recorded as features; height about the third percentile is recorded as a feature but 'growth failure' is left not reported. Narrow absences (no arthritis, no bloody diarrhea) did not exclude the broader checklist items. Father's abdominal pain and diarrhea were not mapped to 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation'. The NF1 variant is attributed to the infant unambiguously and recorded.
